answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can keep a public atlas of stake-bonded identities: each agent registers one entry by locking a bond that only unlocks after a long cooling period. Peers can challenge entries that look duplicated, and if an audit proves one operator controls several, the bonds are slashed. To an attacker this works like a canyon between identities: crossing from one fake persona to another costs another full bond, so a thousand fakes need a thousand times the locked capital. Like mapping a nebula, the atlas makes hidden clusters of colluding identities visible to everyone.
